cards.family_name: Unique Games and graph approximation hardness

cards.algorithm_and_complexity: Hardness reductions, not optimization algorithms; polynomial time for each fixed error or approximation factor.
cards.assumptions: Fixed unweighted simple bipartite translation game over F_2^s; graph results require exact simple/unweighted/loopless problem models; nonexistence conclusions are conditional on P != NP.
cards.proof_dependencies: UG: parity/3Lin gap, matrix shortcode, Fourier/low-rank decoding, Grassmann expansion and alphabet-independent repetition. cards.family_name: Perfect matching counting, entropy, and face dimension
cards.problem_solved: FPRAS for the number of unweighted perfect matchings in an explicit finite simple undirected graph, exact zero on infeasibility; companion pointwise maximum-entropy bounds for feasible perfect-matching edge marginals.
cards.algorithm_and_complexity: Anneal edge activities from a complete graph; estimate adjacent partition ratios; update vertex scales from two-hole ratios to preserve row balance; use subdivisions, tree bags, weak auxiliary edges and marked-edge identities; sample via local switches and alternating-cycle swaps. Worst-case bit time polynomial in input length, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1) on every random tape. Paper says constants prioritize transparent estimates over practical efficiency.
cards.assumptions: Explicit graph, unweighted target matching count, exact perfect-matching feasibility check; entropy theorem assumes a loopless labeled multigraph with 2m vertices and feasible edge marginals. Internal weighted activities are proof/algorithm scaffolding, not arbitrary business-weighted counting.
cards.proof_dependencies: Pairing-capacity bound for even holes; controlled subdivision and auxiliary mass inflation ≤2 under balance; marked-edge two-hole identities; quadrangulation signed-cycle identity; two-coordinate Dirichlet-energy comparison; replicated adjacent tiers to lift coordinate interaction control to the full product-chain spectral gap; exact tree refresh at unit activities; bounded-bit random choices, capped phases and median amplification. Entropy proof uses tight odd-cut contraction/minimal-face geometry, support-codimension control, exponential-family covariance/Hessian and trace bounds.
cards.transferable_principle: Separate feasibility from counting, preserve sampler balance invariants, state the exact counted objects and error model, and distinguish combinatorial entropy from utility or recommendation quality.
lumenis_capability_owner: C1 Collector and Shared Source/Evidence for any candidate identity vocabulary
C5 Reporting/Research only as a method card

cards.family_name: Common bases: matroids and binary-capacity integer polymatroids
cards.source_family_version: OpenAI Math Family 114; openai/math@adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; older paper 2026-09-23, extension 2026-10-05
cards.problem_solved: Older FPRAS counts common bases of two equal-rank matroids from independence oracles. Newer FPRAS counts each integer vector once in the intersection of two integral polymatroid base families with equal total rank and binary capacities, given exact rank-value oracles.
cards.algorithm_and_complexity: New paper partitions binary-scale coordinates into polynomially many partial totals, softens free dimensions, applies log-concavity/Prekopa and rational convex-body volume estimation, smooth weights and discrete quadratic signatures, then two factorial lifts and paired transport/trace/annealing. Oracle calls and external bit operations are polynomial in ground-set size, input bit length, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1), with bounded execution. Oracle's own internal compute cost is excluded; lower-dimensional feasible sets are allowed.
cards.assumptions: Two integral normalized nondecreasing submodular rank functions, equal total rank, finite ground set, exact rank-value oracles, binary capacities. Older result instead has two equal-rank matroids and independence oracles. Counting is unweighted, each feasible base vector once.
cards.proof_dependencies: Integrality of polymatroid base constraints; exact oracle/feasibility behavior; log-concavity of marginals and rational convex-body volume estimates; discrete signatures with curvature; factorial-lift multiplicity cancellation; paired-chain transport and trace bounds; bounded-bit implementation. Large expanded matroids/flows are proof devices; the explicit constructed port pairing is polynomial sized.
cards.transferable_principle: Treat oracle assumptions and their own costs as part of the algorithm contract; prove the combinatorial structure before applying a counting theorem; keep counting separate from finding an optimum.

cards.problem_solved: For nonnegative integer tables with equal-total prescribed row and column margins and no cell caps, provide an exact uniform sampler (almost-sure termination, expected polynomial bit time) and a bounded-time sampler within TV ≤2^-k. A companion FPRAS counts tables with binary-encoded per-cell bounds, including zero bounds, and detects zero exactly.
cards.algorithm_and_complexity: Small-margin cells become explicit states, large rectangle is padded, completion-count law includes paired positive/negative defects; repair bounds defect mass, conditional-fiber quadratic forms and variance decomposition establish mixing. Approximate completion draws use finite scaled grids. Exact sampling corrects the finite sampler law through an extremely rare exhaustive branch: expected-time polynomial, not per-run worst-case bound. Cell-bounded counting uses tightened small/large cell decomposition, capacity forest/free coordinates, paired binary states, factorial lifts/signatures, transport/trace/annealing and rational volume approximation. Counting FPRAS is worst-case polynomial in full binary input, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1); network-flow count and almost-uniform sampling are a separate corollary.
cards.assumptions: Exact sampler permits every nonnegative cell value with fixed equal-total margins; no structural zeros or per-cell caps. Bounded count accepts individual binary bounds including zero cells. Uniformity is conditional on exactly the encoded feasible set and margins.
cards.proof_dependencies: Padding guarantees large completion margins; repair map controls defect mass and unpadding acceptance; quadratic forms with at most one positive eigenvalue survive balanced-pair summation; weighted telescoping and conditional-variance decomposition yield Poincare/mixing; finite-grid completion approximation and TV coupling; rare-law correction gives exact uniformity in expectation. Bounded counting uses binary-encoding-sensitive volume/annealing and finite-bit proofs.
cards.transferable_principle: Define the target population/model before claiming a sample. Uniform over feasible tables conditional on margins is not a sample of real sources and does not establish representativeness.
lumenis_capability_owner: C1 SYSTEM Collector and canonical Source/Evidence path
C3 aggregate reports only when current owners supply the semantics
cards.current_gap: C1 explicitly labels registered-entry coverage and world completeness NOT_ASSERTED and leaves platform_heat/representative_demand null. C5 selects verified task-relevant sources (explicit IDs or latest nonempty, max 8, 1200-character task-term windows) and labels coverage PARTIAL. Neither is a probability sample or a request to sample mathematical tables.
cards.proposed_adaptation: Defer product adoption. If a future approved analysis defines a conditional null model over aggregate tables, use clearly labeled synthetic tables or counts only within that model. Never write synthetic tables as Source, Evidence or Canonical observations or use them to fill missing coverage. For real-world inference first establish a frame, inclusion probabilities, nonresponse and source/platform/time coverage.
cards.required_data: For unbounded exact sampling: equal-total row/column margins and all cells allowed. For bounded counting: every cell bound including zeros plus binary encodings. For real representativeness additionally require target population/frame, unit IDs, inclusion probabilities, time/platform/source coverage, missingness/nonresponse, rights/Permission and provenance.
cards.expected_benefit: Could count feasible aggregate tables under valid bounds or generate a model-specific synthetic null; gives no evidence that observed or generated tables represent the world, a brand, platform, user or country.
cards.computational_cost: Exact unbounded sampler is almost-sure and expected polynomial in dimensions and log(N+1), with no worst-case latency bound; bounded-TV sampler is polynomial in dimensions, log(N+1) and k; cell-bounded counting is worst-case polynomial in full binary encoding, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1). Papers state large exponents and provide no LUMENIS benchmark.
cards.failure_conditions: Unequal margins; wrong allowed cells/caps; interpreting a generated table as an observed record sample, empirical likelihood or representative coverage; using bounded-count theorem as exact bounded sampler; or allowing synthetic values into Evidence/Canonical truth/training positives.
cards.rights_license: Repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0; paper READMEs do not state separate manuscript terms. No full-text training. Synthetic output/method card requires separate C2/C5 rights, privacy and evaluation review.
cards.validation_method: Future only: enumerate tiny-margin feasible tables; compare exact counts, sampler law/TV and feasibility; for bounded count compare FPRAS on enumerable instances and test exact-zero. Independently audit real sampling frame, inclusion probabilities, nonresponse and source/time/platform coverage before any representativeness claim. Not performed.
cards.stop_conditions: Stop if the target is actual posts, sources, people, brands, countries or platform coverage rather than conditional table combinatorics; no frame or inclusion probability; cell bounds/structural zeros omitted; or synthetic output could be mistaken for fact or training evidence.
cards.MODEL_LEARNING_scope: Derived non-verbatim algorithm card only, preserving the counterexample that conditional uniform tables are not representative world samples. No paper text or synthetic data admitted and no training run.
cards.MODEL_LEARNING_gates: C2/C5 separately review rights, privacy, provenance, synthetic labels, train/held-out separation, evaluation, versioning, promotion and rollback. Candidate does not equal admission.
cards.concrete_example: Hypothetical conditional null model for a month-by-channel aggregate table with justified fixed margins and allowed cells; generated tables are explicitly synthetic and interpreted only under that null.
cards.counterexample: Generate a country-by-platform table and treat it as real coverage, fill uncollected countries with synthetic counts, or use it as positive training data.
practical_baselines: Min-cost flow for lowest-cost feasible allocation
Documented frame and probability/stratified sampling for real-record inference; IPF is fitting, not uniform sampling
